newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PETULAMA SEES 15 PCT RETURN IN MEDIUM TERM.
newsitem.headline: PETULAMA SEES 15 PCT RETURN IN MEDIUM TERM.

text.p: Premium winemaker Petaluma Wines Ltd said on Thursday a 15 percent net return on shareholders funds was an achieveable target in the medium-term, following a 13.5 percent rise in net profit in 1996/97.

"Petaluma is also intent on building sustainability of profit through the strength of its brands in the ultra premium market, which is as important as the profitability target itself," executive chairman Brian Croser said in a statement.

Croser said Petaluma's net profit, which rose to A$3.46 million in 1996/97 from A$3.05 million in the previous year, had exceeded directors' expectations because of better than budgeted margins and lower interest charges.
Petaluma was selling into the most buoyant market conditions for ultra premium wine experienced in both the domestic and key export markets, he said.

He said fears of premium grape surpluses had been somewhat allayed with most of the large rise in premium varietal plantings in the 'new world' wine regions which include Australia and the Americas not aimed at the ultra premium
"...There is every reason to believe that in the medium term the benchmark of 15 percent after tax return on shareholders funds is an achievable target for Petaluma Ltd," he said.

Croser said Petaluma had made a number of land and vineyard purchases in the Clare, Piccadilly and Goulburn valleys and the Coonawarra which would allow growth into the ultra premium market beyond 2000.
